title: Stonepine Systems hosting exit + compatibility discovery
summary: Introductory discovery: Stonepine is evaluating exit from OpenAI-hosted endpoints toward a mix of Redwood Hosted or Dedicated with a later Private option. Primary concerns: eval parity with current OpenAI/chat-based models, vLLM/TGI compatibility for on-prem pilot, data residency, KMS/HSM for keys, SSO/SAML and RBAC, and predictable latency at peak. They want a 4-week pilot with benchmarks and a secure architecture proposal.
topics: hosting vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
action_items: Maya Chen: Send tailored pilot proposal with pricing bands and SLA bullets (due: 2026-10-08)
Diego Alvarez: Share vLLM/TGI compatibility checklist and recommended quantization profiles (due: 2026-10-06)
Priya Nair: Provision a short eval repo with sample prompts and ingestion scripts (due: 2026-10-07)
Amir Patel: Share current prompt sets and three representative evals (due: 2026-10-05)
next_steps: Redwood to run parity benchmarks (latency/cost/quality) on customer prompts vs OpenAI baseline
Security follow-up with Ravi to review SOC2 bits and KMS/HSM options
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-03 16:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Amir Patel (Stonepine Head of ML), Lena Ortiz (Platform Eng), Ravi Menon (Security), Tom (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto): Stonepine exploring exit from OpenAI for cost predictability and data control. Interested in Redwood Hosted for fast rails but Dedicated for predictability and a future Private/VPC for regulated datasets. Wants parity checks for OpenAI chat completions and on-prem runtime compatibility with vLLM/TGI stacks.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros, uh, we'll go over why you're evaluating an exit and what success looks like.
[00:18] Amir: Thanks Maya. Yeah, we currently run most customer-facing features on OpenAI, we're seeing cost creep and also audit requests around logs and retention. We're looking at options — hosted vs dedicated vs private — and want to understand the migration effort.
[00:36] Diego: Got it. Quick clarifying q - are you using embeddings + text-gen + chat completions, or a subset?
[00:44] Amir: Embeddings for search, chat completions for inbox assistant, and an internal reranker. Also some fine-tuned-ish patterns via prompt engineering. We also have a small on-prem research rig where we run vLLM/TGI experiments.
[01:05] Lena: To add, our infra team needs predictable latency at peak and the ability to isolate traffic from prod when we run experiments.
[01:13] Priya: Understood. Can you share rough qps and payload sizes?
[01:17] Tom: Peak is about 60 qps for gen endpoints, typical sequence 1-2k tokens per conv, embeddings batch sizes of 32.
[01:28] Maya: That's helpful. Two axes to consider: 1) Hosted to replace OpenAI right away for minimal change; 2) Dedicated for committed capacity if you need guaranteed throughput; 3) Private later if you need VPC/HSM and full control.
[01:45] Amir: Costwise OpenAI is getting expensive at scale, but the trick is eval parity — we can't afford quality regressions. How do you ensure the models Redwood hosts match the OpenAI outputs?
[01:58] Diego: Good question. We approach parity in three ways — model selection and mapping, prompt translation and function mirroring, and evals. We run prompt-based A/Bs on your actual prompt sets and produce quality metrics (ROUGE/ BLEU are noisy for chat so we use human evals + automated rubric). For models that aren't identical we provide fallback routing to the hosted upstream until you're comfortable. Also we keep track of deterministic seeds when possible, but chat is tricky.
[02:28] Ravi: From security — we need SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC, audit logs and KMS integration (we use AWS KMS + HSM for the most sensitive keys). Any gotchas?
[02:44] Priya: Redwood supports SAML SSO, per-team RBAC, and audit logs. For KMS we integrate with customer KMS; HSM options discussed in Private deployments. We'll surface SOC2 certs and our compliance pack.
[02:58] Lena: How fast is the Dedicated warmup? If we commit capacity, can we scale for bursts?
[03:05] Diego: Dedicated has predictable throughput with configurable autoscaling and burst options. Warmup is usually handled by pre-warmed workers; if you commit a pool size we can keep a margin.
[03:15] Amir: About vLLM/TGI — we run internal experiments on TGI and some community models via vLLM. If we want to run some inference on-prem later, how compatible is Redwood's runtime with those tooling choices?
[03:28] Maya: We support deploying model artifacts via a common model catalog. For Private on-prem, we can run the Redwood control plane locally and the serving runtime supports vLLM/TGI-flavored checkpoints in most cases, but we'll need to validate operator-level bits like quantization format, fused kernels, and KV cache handling.
[03:50] Diego: Real-world note: sometimes the Hugging Face checkpoint converted for vLLM has different positional encodings or custom ops; we have a conversion checklist. We'll share it. For on-prem TGI setups we work with the same kernel graph, but quantization profiles might differ — that's why we recommend a small porting eval.
[04:12] Amir: Good. Regarding benchmarks, can you run our prompts and compare token latency and cost vs OpenAI?
[04:20] Priya: Absolutely. For hosted parity we'll run the existing prompt set through both OpenAI and the Redwood-hosted model variants and produce latency distributions, token counts, and a quality score. We'll also estimate cost per 1M tokens given batching and prefix caching.
[04:36] Tom: Do you support KV cache reuse across sessions for chat to save tokens?
[04:40] Diego: Yes, we have prefix and KV caching that can be persisted for sessions. That feeds into cost reductions and lower latencies.
[04:49] Ravi: For compliance, do you provide immutable audit logs and the ability to purge data on request?
[04:55] Priya: We can produce audit logs, and Private deployments give you full control over retention. Hosted/Dedicated have configurable retention policies and we provide deletion APIs and attestations.
[05:08] Lena: Any limits on prompt length or attachment size?
[05:11] Diego: Model-specific. We'll map your payloads to the recommended sequence length and show options: truncation, windowing, or chunking for long docs.
[05:20] Amir: Another practical — we do function calling and structured outputs heavily. Do you support function/tool calling and structured JSON responses reliably?
[05:28] Priya: Yes, we support streaming outputs, function calling semantics, and structured output enforcement via output schemas. We also do reranking and embeddings natively.
[05:40] Maya: Let's talk timeline. Are you looking to pilot immediately?
[05:44] Amir: ASAP. Ideally a short 4-week pilot where you host our prompt set, we run parity tests, and we evaluate proxy costs. If that passes, we'd commit to Dedicated for 6-12 months then plan Private for regulated bundles.
[05:58] Diego: That's a common path. For the pilot we'll need three representative eval suites, sample data, and an integration point. We'll produce a pilot runbook and acceptance criteria.
[06:12] Ravi: Security follow-up — we want to schedule a 30-min security deep dive with your security engineer.
[06:18] Maya: Great, we'll get Ravi's meeting set. Diego, can you own the vLLM/TGI checklist?
[06:23] Diego: Yup, will do.
[06:25] (some cross talk)
[06:40] Amir: Quick question on SLAs and failure modes — if a model variant falls behind quality during a rollout how do you fallback?
[06:47] Diego: We have routing policies and automatic fallback to a compatible variant or upstream (e.g., upstream OpenAI if you opt in). For Dedicated we also support canary/A-B rollouts and auto-fallback on error/latency thresholds.
[06:59] Tom: Do you provide per-token cost breakouts by endpoint? We need to attribute to internal teams.
[07:04] Priya: Yes, the Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route metrics, and per-model latency histograms.
[07:12] Amir: Any migration gotchas for fine-tuned prompts vs OpenAI's fine-tuning?
[07:18] Diego: If you're relying on OpenAI fine-tunes, mapping to an open model may require prompt-engineered shim layers or a distilled fine-tune on our side. We'll measure delta and recommend either prompt templates or a retrain.
[07:33] Lena: For networking, if we want VPC peering or private link, doable?
[07:37] Priya: Yes for Private deployments we support VPC and on-prem. For Dedicated we can provide private connectivity options depending on region and account setup.
[07:46] Ravi: Are there any hidden egress costs in Dedicated or Private?
[07:50] Maya: Egress depends on deployment topology. We'll include that in the pilot proposal with estimated bandwidth fees.
[07:58] Amir: Cool. Let's capture next steps.
[08:02] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send pilot proposal + pricing, Diego shares vLLM/TGI checklist and quant profiles, Priya sets up eval repo, Stonepine shares prompts and sample traffic. We'll also schedule a security deep dive and pilot kickoff.
[08:20] Amir: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-hears: 'KVM' seen in notes refers to KMS, 'TGI' sometimes transcribed 'tee-gee-eye', speaker labels sometimes shifted. Natural speech, pauses, and filler words present.
notes: Customer is pragmatic: wants low lift first (hosted parity) with the option to move to Dedicated/Private. Main drivers: cost predictability, auditability, compliance. Strong interest in vLLM/TGI compatibility for on-prem research workloads. They asked for a 4-week pilot and security deep dive.
